clue.text: Prime minister and team in talks get fine wine

parts.note: the Prime Minister is often called the Premier

indicators.note: in talks means spoken, so the word for team is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a team of rowers or workers is a crew

explanation.surface: A head of government and colleagues at a summit are rewarded with an expensive bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in talks' turns CREW into its sound-alike CRU, the French word for a vineyard's growth, as in premier cru.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier cru is the French classification for a top-ranking vineyard, so the label marks a quality wine.

clue.text: Dispel misgivings of engineers over a ship on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the engineers come above the rest

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
SS is short for steamship
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Army engineers calm the nerves of a crew on a vessel moored on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means placed above, so the engineers head the column. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone's doubts to rest is to comfort them, a straight synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Plan that has mother and father joined in opposition?

parts.note: Ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: joined says the two words are fused, sharing the letter where they meet
in opposition means facing the other way, so the word for father is turned round

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A political scheme involving parents who sit together on the opposition benches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in opposition' turns the father round so the two parents stand back to back; 'joined' fuses them where they touch, so the shared A is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: A map is a chart or layout, and a plan is a drawing of the same kind.

clue.text: Finish serving first of ewes with a ram

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word ewes

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a word used by British sheep farmers

explanation.surface: A farmer's helping of food is done with once the ewes are put to the ram.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a British farming word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume a whole portion of food is to clear the plate, the sense of finishing a helping.

clue.text: Girl seasick in yacht

indicators.note: a seasick sailor is churned up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman feels queasy aboard a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasick' looks like a description of the girl, but it signals that IN YACHT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynthia is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: City of atlantis? All believe this but it may not be real

definitions.text: All believe this but it may not be real

parts.note: urban means of or belonging to a city
the sunken island of Atlantis is a legend, a story nobody can prove

explanation.surface: A lost city like Atlantis is widely believed in, though it may never have existed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of' is the adjective URBAN; Atlantis, the legendary drowned island, is a MYTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a story everyone repeats and accepts though it is untrue or unproven.

clue.text: Headland facing west in the Pacific

indicators.note: facing west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A promontory pointing towards the setting sun on the Pacific coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' shows the letters lie inside THE PACIFIC; 'facing west' (right to left in an across answer) reads EPAC backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a point of land jutting into the sea, the same as a promontory.

clue.text: Annoyed Titus in school made to do this?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Annoyed Titus in school made to do this?': CROSS (annoyed) + S(TIT)CH needs TIT inside SCH, but the clue gives TITUS and no word removes US; neither a search nor a parse supplies the missing step.
annotationWithheld.clue: Annoyed Titus in school made to do this?

clue.text: Choice of fruit typical of upper class

definitions.meaning: choice as an adjective means desirable or excellent
of or like a soft stone fruit, full of its flavour
describes the rich, plum-in-the-mouth accent of the posh

explanation.definitionFit: Plummy means desirable (a plum job), plum-like in taste or colour, and of a voice, affectedly posh.

clue.text: Alexandra's favourite puritans upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of puritans are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The Tsarina's favourite person caused distress among strict Protestants.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexandra was the last Tsarina of Russia, and the mystic Rasputin was her favoured adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the Russian mystic who won the trust of Tsarina Alexandra, so he was her favourite.

clue.text: It's commonplace in boy's first raise to apply inflation

indicators.note: in puts the word for commonplace inside the other letters
first picks out the opening letter of the word boy's

parts.note: to up a price is to raise it
low can mean common or vulgar

explanation.surface: A boy's first pay rise is swallowed up by rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the commonplace word between the boy's initial and the word for raise; 'It's' at the start merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a balloon or tyre is to inflate it with air.

clue.text: What stripper does turns after first in audience is dozing?

indicators.note: after says that turned word follows the first letter of audience
first in picks out the opening letter of audience
turns says the word for what the stripper does is read the other way round

parts.note: a stripper peels off clothes

explanation.surface: A striptease performer twirls while the audience nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reads the stripper's action backwards to give a word for slumber, which 'after' puts behind the audience's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being asleep is the state of someone nodding off, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Justify having ditched partner over simple game

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the former partner comes above the rest

parts.note: an ex is a former partner who has been dumped
plain means simple, unadorned
an away game is played at the other side's ground

explanation.surface: Someone tries to excuse dumping a partner because of a simple game.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means placed above, so the former partner heads the column. An away game is one played at the opponents' ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something away is to give reasons that excuse it, a way of defending or excusing it.

clue.text: Horse, even more beautiful

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
and some is an idiom meaning and even more besides

explanation.surface: A horse described as even more beautiful than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin, H; 'and some' is the colloquial phrase for 'even more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking, an attractive appearance close in sense to lovely.

clue.text: One making sense of partly scanty letters?

definitions.text: One making sense of partly scanty letters?

indicators.note: making sense of jumbled characters means sorting them into order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who can decipher a message from only a few letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making sense of' signals that PARTLY SCANTY is rearranged; the whole clue also describes a code-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A code-breaker deciphers secret messages, making meaning out of scrambled text.

clue.text: Reinforced FBI agents spread out after gold

indicators.note: after says the agents and the spreading follow the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
G-men is slang for FBI agents
to ted is to spread out hay to dry

explanation.surface: FBI agents fan out to guard a gold reserve, strengthening security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the agents and the spreading behind the gold. To ted is an old farming verb for spreading mown hay to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Augmented means increased or strengthened by addition, the sense of being bolstered.

clue.text: Neighbours at table continue putting out new type of coffee

parts.note: East and South are neighbouring seats at the bridge table

indicators.note: putting out means the letter for new is removed

parts.note: to press on is to continue

explanation.surface: Diners seated together keep going, serving a new kind of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' removes N (new) from PRESS ON; E and S are adjacent seats at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans, one kind of the drink.

clue.text: Dispute rocked rough estates

indicators.note: rocked means shaken, so the letters of rough estates are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quarrel shook the deprived housing developments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocked' signals that ROUGH ESTATES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue the toss is to quarrel over a decision already made, so it means to contest.

clue.text: Unusual sea bird is oriental

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of sea are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A strange seabird turns out to come from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges SEA into EAS, followed by TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern and oriental both describe things from the East, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Key in alarm watch may depend on it

indicators.note: in puts the key inside the word for alarm

parts.note: an alert is a warning signal, an alarm
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Whether a winding key fits the alarm clock decides if it keeps time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B (a musical key) inside ALERT. An albert is a watch chain, named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a chain from which a pocket watch hangs, so the timepiece is suspended from it.

clue.text: Queen invested in fine estates whence a royal mare came

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the queen sits within the other letters

parts.note: estates are lands
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen puts money into fine country estates, home of a royal mare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts the queen inside the other letters. Henry VIII mocked his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, as 'the Flanders mare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne of Cleves came from the Low Countries region and was mocked as a horse from there.

clue.text: Desert girl — she's without a husband

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes around the rest

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman is abandoned, left without her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so SARA wraps round A and H; 'she's' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the vast North African desert, an example of the term.

clue.text: Poles hold caught men in disdain

indicators.note: hold means the poles contain the other letters

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Polish people hold captured soldiers in contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts C and OR (other ranks, soldiers who are not officers) between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain both mean contempt for something thought unworthy.

clue.text: Flighty type receives little backing in trading floor

indicators.note: receives means the trading floor takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a pit is the trading floor of an exchange

indicators.note: backing means the word for little is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A frivolous dealer gets scant support on the exchange floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses WEE to EEW, which PIT 'receives'. A peewit is the lapwing.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, or lapwing, is a bird, so humorously a creature that takes to the air.

clue.text: One who wants to be without monstrous entity

definitions.text: One who wants to be without monstrous entity

parts.words: One who wants to be without monstrous entity
parts.note: describes a priest who wishes a possessed person to be rid of a demon, disguised as someone wanting to be free of a monster

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone who simply wants a monster gone; the person who expels an evil spirit from someone is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist drives demons out of the possessed, ridding them of an evil spirit.

clue.text: Aggressive dog needing a lot of restraint

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word for restraint, with its final letter lost

parts.note: a curb is a restraint or check

explanation.surface: A vicious dog requires a good deal of holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' keeps most of CURB, dropping its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a snappy, ill-bred mongrel, a nasty kind of hound.

clue.text: Remain in support

definitions.meaning: to remain is to stop on rather than leave
a prop or brace, such as a rope steadying a mast

explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to linger; a stay is also a prop or brace holding something steady.

clue.text: Man at wedding follows noise inside refectory

indicators.note: follows says the man at the wedding comes after the other letters

parts.note: din is a loud noise
in means inside
the groom is the man getting married at a wedding

explanation.surface: The bridegroom comes after the racket indoors at the reception hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the bridegroom after the noise and the word for inside; read that way 'inside' is a plain piece, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a communal hall for meals, as in a college or monastery, where people eat.
